name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Hari Tua (old-age savings)

configuration.limitation: PP 46/2015 art.16 — 5.7% of the monthly wage, 2% from the employee and 3.7% from the employer. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AO5` = 2% (employee) and `!AR5` = 3.7% (employer); `!AE5` prints the combined 5.7%. NO CEILING: the highest-paid local employee, basic 22,380,750, is charged `AO17` 447,615 = 2% of the FULL wage, and the one foreign employee at 62,000,000 is charged `AK6` 1,240,000 = 2% of the full wage. Both would be clamped if any ceiling applied, and neither is. PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. PP 46/2015 art.17(3): wages paid by the day make a month of the day’s wage × 25, whatever days were paid (`person.terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY"`). Owner rule 2026-09-28: PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) and PP 46/2015 art.17(1)–(2) charge JKK, JKM and JHT on “Upah sebulan” — upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap as a monthly rate — and, unlike PP 45/2015 art.29(1) for JP, do not say “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”; so a monthly-paid worker's base is the contract's monthly rate (`person.terms.monthly_wage`: the basic plus the contract allowances counting toward this scheme, on the terms in force on the month's last employed day), whatever days were paid — a joiner, a leaver and a month with unpaid days are charged on the whole rate. The law is silent on an hourly-paid worker (art.19(3)–(5) name only daily, piece and weather-bound piece wages); default: the wage paid for the month's hours. Piece-rate wages use the average paid wage of the preceding 3 months, or 12 months where work depends on weather (PP 44/2015 art.19(4)–(5), PP 46/2015 art.17(4)–(5)); only months of this employment count. The first month uses the current paid wage. a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; PP 46/2015 art.2(1) obliges the employer to register every worker for JHT, art.9(2) runs the contribution from the day the worker starts, and art.11(4) makes a negligent employer pay the contribution it owed. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Pensiun (pension)

configuration.limitation: PP 45/2015 art.28 — 3% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 2% from the employer, charged on wage up to an annually adjusted ceiling (art.29). The ceiling is 11,086,300 from 1 March 2026 (SE BPJS Ketenagakerjaan No. B/1226/022026 of 25 February 2026, the art.29(3) uplift by 2025 GDP growth of 5.11%). SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AN5` = 1% (employee) and `!AQ5` = 2% (employer); `!AF5` prints the combined 3%. The ceiling and its March step are read off the one employee it binds — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. JP covers Indonesian nationals only (the rule `when`). The one foreign employee is charged 0 in both `AJ6` and `AM6` on every (FOREIGN) sheet while still paying JHT, JKK, JKM and Kesehatan. Nationality is not a `rate_selector` axis; it belongs on employment_statutory_facts — see ID_JP_FOREIGN_EXCLUSION. PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. PP 45/2015 art.15(1)–(3): the pension age is 56, 57 from 1 January 2019 and one year more every three years — 59 from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027; art.15(4): a participant who is still employed may choose to take the pension when work stops, at most three years after pension age. Contributions stop at 59 unless that choice is recorded (`scheme.elections.continue_after_pension_age`, to 62). a missing registration does not waive JP (`unregistered_action` ASSESS, with a registration-incomplete warning). PP 45/2015 art.4(1)–(2) makes registration of every worker mandatory within 30 days of starting work, and art.5(5) obliges the negligent employer to collect and pay both the worker's and its own contributions besides the art.5(4) sanction; art.3(1) dates the start of benefit protection, and art.6 adds the employer's own liability for the benefit meanwhile — neither removes the contribution. A foreign national cannot be registered for JP (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan), so the rule `when` charges a foreigner only on a recorded registration and a NOT_REGISTERED foreigner stays at 0. each contribution month is priced on its own wage (art.28–29(1), “pada bulan yang bersangkutan”), so a deferred earlier month paid here as back pay (`person.period.arrears`, a joiner after the cut-off) is capped at the ceiling on its own beside this month’s wage, not merged into one capped base.

name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja (work accident)

refuse_when.message: record the company's JKK risk group (I to V) — PP 44/2015 art.16(1).

configuration.limitation: PP 44/2015 art.16(1) and Lampiran I: employer-only JKK by the employer's work-risk group (`company.risk_class`): I very low 0.24%, II low 0.54%, III medium 0.89%, IV high 1.27%, V very high 1.74% of the monthly wage. PP 37/2021 art.11 as amended by PP 6/2025: 0.14% of the wage is recomposed from the JKK contribution to JKP — an internal allocation, not a cut in the employer's bill. The base is the contract's monthly rate (owner rule 2026-09-28: PP 44/2015 art.19(1)–(2) "Upah sebulan"); a daily worker's month is the wage paid. A company without a recorded risk group is refused (no default group).

name: BPJS Kesehatan (health insurance)

configuration.limitation: Perpres 82/2018 art.30 as amended — 5% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 4% from the employer, charged on wage between a floor and a ceiling (Perpres 59/2024 art.32(1) and (2) — the third amendment, in force 8 May 2024 — restating the ceiling and floor; art.31 was deleted by Perpres 64/2020 and art.30(2) is the direct-payment rule). For PPU outside micro/small enterprises, art.32(2)–(3) sets the workplace UMK, with UMP as fallback; art.32(4) excludes micro/small enterprises from that floor, and art.32(5) requires a separately determined actuarial floor; `by_region` carries the Kabupaten Bekasi UMK (Kepgub Jabar 2026) beside the UMP, and the company’s region names it, so the floor is the workplace UMK. SOURCE: `JAN 2026 (LOCAL)!AP5` = 1% (employee) and `!AU5` = 4% (employer); `!AG5` prints the combined 5%. The 12,000,000 ceiling is read off two employees — see ID_BPJS_CEILINGS_OBSERVED. The art.30(2) FLOOR is carried by `FLOOR:MINIMUM_WAGE` against this version's `minimum_wages` map, which `company.region` keys; the source is silent on it, the lowest basic salary anywhere in the workbook being 5,938,885, so no row in the source is floored. Perpres 82/2018 art.5(3)–(4) and art.36: a further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the wage each, paid by the worker; carried as a rate override on the registration, never charged from the household count. One employee pays exactly 2% in every month; a dependant count is not a `rate_selector` axis. See ID_KESEHATAN_EXTRA_FAMILY_MEMBERS. art.5(3)–(4) and art.36: a further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the wage each, paid by the worker; carried as a rate override on the registration, never charged from the household count. EMPLOYEE_PER_DEPENDANT:20:4 charges one more employee share per head past those four; the regulation states no ceiling, so 20 is a nominal one no household reaches. PP 44/2015 art.19(2), PP 45/2015 art.29(1), PP 46/2015 art.17(1), Perpres 82/2018 art.32: the contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base (`ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward)); a reimbursement is not. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. Perpres 82/2018 art.1 angka 2: a participant is every person, a foreigner included, who works at least six months in Indonesia — the same six-month reading JHT, JKK and JKM apply (PP 44/2015 art.1 angka 4): a foreigner on a contract shorter than six months is outside Kesehatan. a missing registration does not waive this charge (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) obliges the employer to register itself and its workers “dengan membayar Iuran”, art.13(5) leaves the health benefit on an employer that has not registered and paid, and art.14(1) requires each spouse's employer to register and pay. A recipient paid outside an employment relationship — a PMK 168/2023 bukan pegawai (NON_EMPLOYEE, IRREGULAR_COMMISSIONER, ACTIVITY_PARTICIPANT), a former employee or a pension withdrawal — is not a wage-earning worker of this employer: PP 44/2015 art.5(2)–(3) and PP 46/2015 art.4(2)–(3) make a worker outside an employment relationship a non-wage-earning participant who registers and pays for himself (PP 44/2015 art.11(1)), and Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) binds the employer only for its Pekerja; so that recipient class charges nothing, the lawful exclusion a NOT_REGISTERED record no longer stands in for. the contribution is monthly (Perpres 82/2018 art.30, art.32(1) “per bulan”), so a deferred earlier month paid here as back pay (`person.period.arrears`, a joiner after the cut-off) is floored and capped at 12,000,000 on its own beside this month’s wage, not merged into one capped base. Owner rule 2026-09-30 (Perpres 82/2018 arts.30(1), 32(1)–(2) price “Gaji atau Upah per bulan” with the UMK/UMP as its lowest bound and are silent on a part month): the base is the wage paid for the month — basic plus fixed allowances less unpaid days, the same month’s-wage reading as JP (PP 45/2015 art.29(1)) — and a month’s wage paid below the floor is lifted to the whole floor, not a prorated one; so a joiner, a leaver or a month with unpaid days whose wage paid is under the UMK is charged on the UMK (a joiner on 16 February 2026 at 12,000,000, paid 5,571,428.57 under the DKI UMP 5,729,876: 57,299 / 229,195), and a deferred joiner month paid as back pay is lifted the same way on its own. Perpres 82/2018 art.30(1)(b) and art.36: each further family member a worker enrols (the KESEHATAN election `extra_members`) adds 1% of the same capped wage, borne by the worker. Perpres 82/2018 art.32(2)–(5) as amended by Perpres 59/2024: outside a micro or small enterprise (`company.facts.enterprise_size_class`) the wage is never taken below the workplace minimum wage — the UMK, or the UMP where no UMK is set — read from `rules.minimum_wage.by_region[company.region]`; a company whose region is not a key there is refused.

UU 24/2011 art.15(1) and art.19(1)–(2) oblige the employer to register its workers and to collect and pay the contribution; Perpres 82/2018 art.13(1) obliges the employer to register itself and its workers “dengan membayar Iuran”, art.13(5) leaves the health benefit on an employer that has not registered and paid, and art.14(1) requires each spouse's employer to register and pay. configuration.limitation: PP 37/2021 Pasal 11 as amended by PP 6/2025: the JKP contribution is 0.36% of the wage capped at Rp5,000,000 (Pasal 11(7)–(8)), of which 0.22% is the central government's and 0.14% is recomposed out of the JKK contribution the employer already pays; nothing is charged on a payslip beyond JKK. Only that recomposed 0.14% is an employer charge: JKK class III 0.75 + JKM 0.30 + JKP 0.14 = 1.19% of wage, the same total the source workbook's 0.89 + 0.30 charges; only the composition of the payslip lines moves. Where the KDIT listing charged the wage alone (JHT on 22,380,750 for KDIT0002), the law charges 27,880,750. PP 37/2021 art.4 as amended by PP 6/2025 art.I(1) requires an Indonesian worker under 54 at registration who has an employment relationship and the prescribed JKK/JHT/JKM/JKN (and, at medium/large employers, JP) coverage. configuration.limitation: PP 58/2023 art.2–3 and PMK 168/2023 arts.12–13 with Lampiran A (tarif efektif rata-rata bulanan): for each tax period other than the last, PPh 21 of a permanent employee is the month's gross income (penghasilan bruto, all regular and irregular pay of the month, PMK 168/2023 art.5(1), including the employer-paid JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums; the employer's JHT and JP shares are not income) times the TER rate of the employee's category for that gross: category A = PTKP TK/0, TK/1, K/0; B = TK/2, TK/3, K/1, K/2; C = K/3 (PP 58/2023 art.3(4)–(6)). Every bracket of tables A (44 brackets, 0% to Rp5,400,000 up to 34% above Rp1,400,000,000), B (40, 0% to Rp6,200,000 up to 34% above Rp1,405,000,000) and C (41, 0% to Rp6,600,000 up to 34% above Rp1,419,000,000) is transcribed from the PP 58/2023 Lampiran as reproduced in the PMK 168/2023 annex, upper bounds inclusive ("s.d."). The last tax period — December, or the month a permanent employee stops working (PMK 168/2023 art.13) — takes the year's tax at the UU PPh art.17(1)(a) rates as amended by UU 7/2021 (5% to Rp60,000,000; 15% to Rp250,000,000; 25% to Rp500,000,000; 30% to Rp5,000,000,000; 35% above) on penghasilan kena pajak rounded down to the full thousand: the year's gross less biaya jabatan (5%, at most Rp6,000,000 a year, PMK 168/2023 art.10 and PMK 250/2008 as carried into PMK 168/2023), less the employee's own JHT and JP contributions, less PTKP (Rp54,000,000; +Rp4,500,000 married; +Rp4,500,000 per dependant, at most three — UU PPh art.7(1) as amended by UU 7/2021, PMK 101/2016), and withholds that tax less the TER already withheld in the year; an excess is returned to the employee in that period (a negative charge). A married female employee takes TK/0 unless she holds a kelurahan statement that her husband has no income (`employee.facts.husband_no_income_certified`). Residents only: CITIZEN and RESIDENT_FOREIGNER; a NON_RESIDENT is taxed under PPh 26. Parts: `ordinary` and `additional` are the month's cash gross (the line's base). The employer JKK, JKM and Kesehatan premiums and the employee's JHT and JP are read from the schemes' own charges (`charged.month`, `charged.year` — those schemes come first in the catalogue), and the TER already withheld from `charged.year.PPH21.employee`. PMK 168/2023 (official text, https://jdih.kemenkeu.go.id/download/e60a82e0-b218-40f5-9d18-b924aa1e11ce/2023pmkeuangan168.pdf): art.10(2) and the Lampiran worked examples cap biaya jabatan at Rp500,000 for each month worked in the tax year ("maksimal 4 X Rp500.000,00" for a September joiner; `person.months` from the later of 1 January, `employment.start_date` and the tax-subject start). Art.10(1)(c): zakat or a compulsory religious contribution paid through the employer is deducted (customer input `employee.facts.zakat_monthly`). Art.15(3): where the subjective tax obligation starts after January or ends before December (`terms.facts.tax_subject_from` / `tax_subject_until`, e.g. a foreigner arriving or leaving Indonesia), the net income is annualised (× 12 / months) and the tax prorated (× months / 12); the month the subject status ends is the last tax period. Art.12(2)(b), 16(2)(b) and Lampiran III.1.5(b): a daily worker above Rp2,500,000 a day is taxed at the art.17(1)(a) rates on 50% of each day's gross. Not modelled: PPh 21 DTP (PMK 10/2025, PMK 105/2025).

name: PPh 21 final atas uang pesangon

configuration.limitation: PP 68/2009 art.2–4: severance pay (uang pesangon, uang penghargaan masa kerja) paid at once is subject to a final PPh 21 — 0% to Rp 50,000,000, 5% to 100,000,000, 15% to 500,000,000, 25% above — separately from the monthly TER withholding; the tiers accumulate over payments within two years, which this row reads as one payment. PP 68/2009 art.1 angka 4 defines uang pesangon as income paid, under whatever name and in whatever form, in connection with the end of service or termination, including UPMK and UPH; uang pisah is paid only on termination (PP 35/2021 arts.50–54), so it is in this final base and outside the TER. uang kompensasi PKWT is paid when the fixed-term agreement ends (PP 35/2021 art.15(2)), in connection with the end of service, so it is in this final base too. the uang penggantian hak PP 68/2009 art.1 angka 4 names includes untaken, unlapsed annual leave (PP 35/2021 art.40(4)(a)), so leave cashed out on or after the last day of work (`ENCASHMENT` once `employment.exit_date` has passed) is in this final base and out of the PPH21 TER/annual base; an in-service cash-out stays ordinary income. PP 68/2009 (signed text: https://jdih.kemnaker.go.id/asset/data_puu/PP_No_68_2009.pdf): the four uang pesangon bands are art.4 (art.5 is the two-band scale for pension benefit, THT and JHT). Art.1 angka 3 limits “Pegawai” to a resident individual, so a non-resident’s separation pay is PPh 26 at 20% of gross (PMK 168/2023 arts.5(1), 12(9), 14(1)), not this row. Art.2(2) and its elucidation (“dihitung sebagai satu kesatuan untuk pengenaan pajaknya”): payments made within two calendar years count as paid at once, so the bands run on this employer’s severance base of the previous and current calendar years (`scheme.last_year`, `scheme.year_to_date`) plus this one, less what those payments already withheld. PP 68/2009 art.6(1)–(3) and its elucidation: a part paid in the third calendar year or later, counted from the tax year of this employer’s first charged severance base (`scheme.first_year`), is not joined to the earlier parts: it is withheld at the UU PPh art.17(1)(a) rates as amended by UU 7/2021 on the gross of that calendar year’s parts (`scheme.year_to_date` plus this one), less what that year already withheld; that withholding is not final and is creditable as a prepayment in the recipient’s annual return (art.6(2)), and art.21(5a)’s 120% applies without an NPWP (art.6(3), election `no_tax_id`). Elucidation: 5% × 50,000,000 = 2,500,000, 120% of it = 3,000,000. Ceiling: the year gross is this scheme’s severance parts; other income paid in that year is withheld under PPH21 and is not added (the elucidation’s example assumes none). A new severance after an earlier one (rehire) is joined to it, and counts its third year from it. a missing tax registration does not waive withholding (`unregistered_action` ASSESS; the payslip warns that registration is outstanding). UU PPh art.21(1) puts the withholding on the payer, and art.21(5a) answers a recipient without an NPWP with a rate 20% higher, not with no tax; the declarations this scheme reads are still required.
